title: Moshier lunar ephemeris: tables, mean elements, and series evaluation
description:
Port the Moshier lunar ephemeris (ELP2000-85 adjusted to DE404) from swemmoon.c to Rust. This covers data tables, fundamental arguments, and the full series evaluation. Pure computation — no global state.

## What to build

### 1. Moon data tables (embedded in swemmoon.c)

Small enough to port inline (no script needed):

| Table | Elements | Format |
|-------|----------|--------|
| LR    | 118 terms × 8 cols = 944 shorts | D, l', l, F, lon_coeff, rad_coeff per term |
| MB    | 77 terms × 6 cols | latitude terms |
| LRT   | 38 terms × 8 cols | T-correction longitude/radius |
| BT    | 16 terms × 5 cols | T-correction latitude |
| LRT2  | 25 terms × 6 cols | T²-correction longitude/radius |
| BT2   | 12 terms × 5 cols | T²-correction latitude |

Plus:
- `z[]` — 24 DE404 fitting coefficients (doubles, transcribe exactly)
- Mean element polynomial coefficients (in mean_elements() body)
- Planetary longitude coefficients for perturbation terms (in mean_elements_pl())

All as `const` arrays. Use `i16` for the short tables.

### 2. mean_elements() → MoonFundamentalArgs

Port the fundamental argument computation (swemmoon.c ~line 1763):
- 5 fundamental arguments: l (Moon anomaly), l' (Sun anomaly), D (elongation), F (node distance), Lp (mean longitude)
- Each is a high-precision polynomial in T (centuries from J2000) plus secular corrections from the z[] array
- Additional planetary longitudes (Ve, Ea, Ma, Ju, Sa) for perturbation terms

Return a struct rather than writing to static variables:
```rust
struct MoonFundamentalArgs {
    l: f64,      // Moon mean anomaly
    l_prime: f64, // Sun mean anomaly  
    d: f64,      // Mean elongation
    f: f64,      // Mean distance from node
    lp: f64,     // Mean longitude of Moon
    // planetary longitudes for perturbation terms
    ve: f64, ea: f64, ma: f64, ju: f64, sa: f64,
}
```

### 3. Series evaluation: moon1–moon4 combined into moshmoon2

The C code splits across moon1()–moon4() accumulating into static TLS variables. Combine into a single function (or keep the split for readability) using a local accumulator:

```rust
struct MoonAccum {
    l: f64,         // longitude accumulator
    b: f64,         // latitude accumulator  
    moonpol: [f64; 3], // [lon, lat, dist]
}
```

The moon functions walk the term tables (LR, MB, etc.) and accumulate:
- `coefficient × sin(n₁×l + n₂×l' + n₃×D + n₄×F + corrections)`
- Polynomial-in-T amplitudes for the correction tables

Core function: `moshmoon2(jd) → [f64; 3]` returning geocentric ecliptic [lon, lat, dist] in radians and AU (or Earth radii — check c-ref-moshier.md for units).

### 4. Golden tests

Write a C generator (`tests/c-gen/gen_moshier_moon.c`) that:
- Calls `swi_moshmoon2()` for the Moon at multiple test epochs
- Test epochs: J2000, J2000±0.5yr, ±1yr, ±10yr, ±100yr, ±500yr, ±1000yr, ±3000yr
- Outputs JSON with [{jd, lon, lat, dist}]
- Moon moves fast, so include some closely-spaced epochs too

Write Rust golden tests in `tests/golden/moshier_moon.rs`.
Assert bitwise-exact (deterministic math, no iteration).

## Architecture notes

- All functions are pure. No &self, no Ephemeris.
- `moshmoon2(jd: f64) -> [f64; 3]` — the only public function needed.
- The moon1-4 split is an implementation detail — keep if it aids readability, combine if it doesn't.
- The `chewm()` helper from C may be shared with the planetary series — check c-ref-moshier.md. If identical, put in a shared location within the moshier module.

## File placement

- `src/moshier/moon.rs` — moshmoon2, mean_elements, series evaluation, data tables
- If tables are large enough to warrant splitting: `src/moshier/moon_tables.rs`
- `tests/c-gen/gen_moshier_moon.c` — C golden data generator
- `tests/golden-data/moshier_moon.json` — generated golden data
- `tests/golden/moshier_moon.rs` — Rust golden tests

## C source reference
- swemmoon.c:848–868 — swi_moshmoon2 entry point
- swemmoon.c:1763–1819 — mean_elements
- swemmoon.c:1820–1930 — mean_elements_pl
- swemmoon.c:205–720 — data tables (LR, MB, LRT, BT, LRT2, BT2, z[])
- swemmoon.c moon1()–moon4() — series evaluation functions
- See docs/c-ref-moshier.md for detailed algorithm documentation

## Dependencies
- Independent of swisseph-rs/24–25 (planet tables/series). Can be implemented in parallel.
- Uses crate::constants::STR and math utilities from Phase 0.

acceptance_criteria.text: All moon term tables ported as const arrays with correct element counts
z[] fitting coefficients transcribed exactly (24 doubles)
mean_elements returns a struct, no static/TLS state
C golden data generator produces JSON at ≥10 test epochs
Golden tests pass bitwise-exact for Moon position at all test epochs
No global state anywhere in the module

execution_record: Implemented as planned with no divergence. Three parallel agents handled: (1) codegen script for moon tables, (2) C source extraction for moon1/moon2 perturbation amplitudes, (3) golden data C generator. All 11 golden tests passed bitwise-exact on first compile — no debugging needed. The z[] array has 25 elements (z[0]..z[24]), not 24 as stated in the acceptance criteria; followed the C source.
